claims.claim: Direct-to-storage upload via pre-signed URLs keeps file bytes off the app server
claims.evidence: Standard, correct S3 pre-signed PUT pattern; consistently applied across Overview, AD-01, and CAP-02 mapping.

claims.claim: sharp handles image thumbnails but not PDF rasterization
claims.evidence: Accurate — sharp/libvips does not rasterize PDFs; correctly flagged as a gap needing a rasterizer (L109, L124).

claims.claim: Every capability is supported and every recommended technology is justified
claims.evidence: Capability→Tech mapping covers CAP-01..05 and each tech choice carries a rationale tied to a capability/constraint.

workarounds: Librarian skill was not available this session; worked from inline breakdown and supplied a retrieval query for librarian-capable agents.

suggestions.reason: This and several other assertions check only for a section heading. A document that emits the heading with empty or boilerplate content would still pass. Consider requiring at least one [stated]/[assumed]-tagged item to ensure substance.

suggestions.assertion: Each tech stack layer gives a Recommendation, a Why/rationale, and at least one Alternative
suggestions.reason: Ambiguous when a layer legitimately has no alternative. Both runs handle it by writing 'None warranted', but the assertion text would mark a layer with a genuine single-option choice as non-compliant. Clarify that an explicit 'no alternative' justification satisfies it.

No assertion checks the 'scan-before-serve' security sequencing (quarantine until clean), which is the single most important correctness property of this architecture. Both runs got it right, but it goes unverified.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are mostly presence/heading checks; they discriminate skill vs baseline well on structure but under-test technical correctness of the design.
